facts.raw_span: left testicular bloating and dull pain for 20 years
acutely worsening over the past 10 days
denied other medical history
left testis was enlarged, firm, smooth, without discrete nodules or tenderness
transillumination was negative
right testis, epididymides, and vas deferens were normal
bilateral epididymal cysts (largest 0.67 × 0.46 cm)
a 1.09 × 0.79 cm well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow
a small left hydrocele
serum CA19-9 level of 57.5 U/mL (normal <27 U/mL)
alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and other tumor markers were within normal limits

concepts.why: A well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow and elevated serum CA19-9 level suggest testicular cancer.
Bilateral epididymal cysts are a common finding, and the largest cyst is 0.67 × 0.46 cm in size.
A small left hydrocele is present, which is a collection of fluid in the scrotum.
Acute worsening of testicular pain and a firm, smooth testis without discrete nodules or tenderness may suggest testicular torsion.
Chronic testicular pain and a firm, smooth testis without discrete nodules or tenderness may suggest orchitis.
A well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow and elevated serum CA19-9 level may suggest seminoma.
A well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow and elevated serum CA19-9 level may suggest non-seminomatous testicular cancer.
Bilateral epididymal cysts and a history of chronic testicular pain may suggest epididymitis.
